chunks: So when you meet the enemy,
stand in the midst of your comrades,
do not draw near to the people with the nearness of one who wants to ignite the war,
nor keep too far from them with the distance of one who fears the combat,
until my command comes to you,
and let not their hatred drive you to fight them,
before inviting them and presenting your excuses to them.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper military etiquette for engaging an enemy according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This directive reflects the strategic prudence and diplomatic rigor characteristic of Imam Ali’s military campaigns, particularly during the Battle of Siffin, where he balanced decisive action with legalistic justification. By mandating a middle ground in positioning and delaying engagement until after the formal stages of invitation (du'a) and justification (i'dhar), the text underscores the Shia principle that war must be a last resort preceded by clear communication of grievances. This approach ensures that the use of force is not driven by emotional retaliation but by structured, legitimate authority.
